In 2026 he had a brief stint with the NBA's Memphis Grizzlies. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola Ramblers]]. ==High school career== Williamson played basketball for [[Whitney M. Young Magnet High School]] in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]]. In his first season, he was the only freshman on the team and won the Class 4A state title alongside [[Jahlil Okafor]].{{cite web |last1=Schnable |first1=Abby |title='More Than an Athlete:' How Lucas Williamson Found His Voice |url=http://loyolaphoenix.com/2019/02/more-than-an-athlete-how-lucas-williamson-found-his-voice/ |website=[[Loyola Phoenix]] |access-date=March 22, 2021 |date=February 27, 2019}} As a senior, Williamson averaged 17.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game, leading his team to another Class 4A state title.{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Freshman spark plug Lucas Williamson: 'I could tell big things were in Loyola's future' |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-lucas-williamson-ncaa-tournament-20180320-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=March 22, 2021 |date=March 20, 2018}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola (Illinois)]] over offers from [[UIC Flames men's basketball|UIC]] and [[Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball|Northern Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Helfgot |first1=Mike |title=Young's Lucas Williamson chooses Loyola for basketball |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/high-school/ct-spt-0418-basketball-lucas-williamson-loyola-20170417-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=March 22, 2021 |date=April 17, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at Loyola, Williamson averaged 4.7 points and 2.2 rebounds per game, earning [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) All-Freshman and All-Bench Team honors.{{cite web |title=Lucas Williamson – Men's Basketball |url=https://loyolaramblers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/lucas-williamson/1507 |website=Loyola University Chicago Athletics |access-date=March 22, 2021}} He helped 11th-seeded Loyola reach the [[Final Four]] of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Bembry |first1=Jerry |title=For Loyola's Donte Ingram and Lucas Williamson, there's no place like home |url=https://andscape.com/features/for-loyola-chicago-donte-ingram-and-lucas-williamson-theres-no-place-like-home/ |website=[[Andscape]] |access-date=March 22, 2021 |date=March 31, 2018}} Williamson missed about half of his sophomore season with two hand injuries.{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Daniel P. |title=Lucas Williamson is a leader on and off the basketball court |url=https://www.luc.edu/features/stories/athletics/mensbasketball2021lucaswilliamson/ |publisher=[[Loyola University Chicago]] |access-date=March 22, 2021}} He averaged 8.8 points and 5.9 rebounds per game. As a junior, he averaged nine points and 3.3 rebounds per game and was an MVC All-Defensive Team selection. In his senior season, Williamson earned Second Team All-MVC honors and was named MVC Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Hajduk |first1=Gabby |title=Dosunmu faces friend, former rival Lucas Williamson in showdown with Loyola Chicago |url=https://dailyillini.com/sports/2021/03/22/dosunmu-faces-friend-former-rival-lucas-williamson-in-showdown-with-loyola-chicago/ |website=[[The Daily Illini]] |access-date=March 22, 2021 |date=March 22, 2021}} He helped Loyola reach the Sweet 16 of the NCAA Tournament, averaging 8.8 points and 3.9 rebounds per game while shooting 35.9 percent from three-point range. Following the season, Williamson took advantage of the extra season of eligibility granted by the NCAA due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Lucas Williamson is 1 of 4 Loyola seniors to announce his return for an extra season of eligibility — a boost for new coach Drew Valentine |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-loyola-lucas-williamson-seniors-return-drew-valentine-20210423-dmksjvcffjd4vi6mwflldv2pce-story.html |access-date=October 6, 2021 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=April 23, 2021}} He earned First Team All-MVC honors and was named MVC Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://mvc-sports.com/news/2022/2/28/arch-madness-aj-green-of-uni-headlines-2022-mvc-mbb-all-conference-teams.aspx |title=AJ Green of UNI Headlines 2022 MVC MBB All-Conference Teams|publisher=[[Missouri Valley Conference]] |date=March 1, 2022 |accessdate=March 1, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Ontario Clippers (2022–2023)=== On June 24, 2022, Williamson signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |title=Lucas Williamson Signs With Los Angeles Clippers|url=https://loyolaramblers.com/news/2022/6/24/mens-basketball-lucas-williamson-signs-with-los-angeles-clippers.aspx |website=Loyola University Chicago Athletics |date=June 24, 2022|access-date=September 10, 2022}} On October 4, Williamson (along with [[Juwan Morgan]] and [[Michael Devoe]]) was waived by the Clippers.{{cite web |title=Clippers re-sign Malik Fitts, add Nate Darling, release three others|url=https://www.clipsnation.com/2022/10/5/23389848/los-angeles-clippers-re-sign-malik-fitts-nate-darling-release-three-others-training-camp-roster-nba#:~:text=LA%20Clippers%20announce%20that%20they,Juwan%20Morgan%20and%20Lucas%20Williamson.&text=Both%20Devoe%20and%20Williamson%20went,selected%20during%20the%202019%20draft.|website=Clips Nation |date=October 5, 2022|access-date=October 7, 2022}} On October 24, Williamson joined the [[Ontario Clippers]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ontario-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2022-23-nba-g-league-season/n-5893040|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Ontario Clippers Announce Training Camp Roster for 2022-23 NBA G League Season|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Edmonton Stingers (2023)=== On March 15, 2023, Williamson signed with the [[Edmonton Stingers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Stingers Sign Lucas Williamson|url=https://www.cebl.ca/stingers-sign-lucas-williamson|website=CEBL.com|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} ===Memphis Hustle (2023–2026)=== On October 30, 2023, Williamson joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2023-24 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 6, 2023}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026)=== On March 31, 2026, Williamson was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Lucas Williamson: Inks 10-day deal with Memphis|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-lucas-williamson-inks-10-day-deal-with-memphis/|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On April 6, Williamson made his first career start, recording 17 points, five rebounds, four assists, and three steals as the Grizzlies lost to the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]], 142–126.{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Lucas Williamson: Sinks five threes in Monday's start|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-lucas-williamson-sinks-five-threes-in-mondays-start/|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On April 10, Williamson re-signed with Memphis on a second 10-day contract.{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies Sign Lucas Williamson to Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-lucas-williamson-to-second-10-day-contract|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} He made seven appearances (including two starts) for the Grizzlies during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 10.4 points, 5.4 points, and 2.6 assists. ===Start Lublin (2026–present)=== On July 30, 2026, he signed with [[Start Lublin]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).{{Cite web|url=https://www.startlublin.pl/aktualnosci/lucas-williamson-w-pge-starcie-lublin|title=Lucas Williamson w PGE Starcie Lublin
